 <modelVersion>
  4.0.0
 </modelVersion>
 <parent>
  <groupId>
   org.sonatype.oss
  </groupId>

   oss-parent
  </artifactId>
  <version>
   7

 <groupId>

 </groupId>
 <artifactId>

 <version>

 <name>

 <description>
  A collection of code generators for Java.

  https://github.com/google/auto

  <project.build.sourceEncoding>
   UTF-8
  </project.build.sourceEncoding>

   http://github.com/google/auto

  <tag>
   HEAD
  </tag>

  <system>
   GitHub Issues
  </system>
  <url>
   http://github.com/google/auto/issues
  </url>
 </issueManagement>
 <licenses>
  <license>
   <name>
    Apache 2.0
   </name>
   <url>
    http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0.txt
   </url>
  </license>
 </licenses>
 <organization>
  <name>
   Google, Inc.
  </name>
  <url>
   http://www.google.com
  </url>
 </organization>
 <build>
  <plugins>
   <plugin>
    <groupId>
     org.apache.maven.plugins
    </groupId>
    <artifactId>
     maven-compiler-plugin
    </artifactId>
    <version>
     3.1
    </version>
    <configuration>
     <source>
      ${java.version}
     </source>
     <target>
      ${java.version}
     </target>
     <compilerArgument>
      -Xlint:all
     </compilerArgument>
     <showWarnings>
      true
     </showWarnings>
     <showDeprecation>
      true
     </showDeprecation>
    </configuration>
   </plugin>
   <plugin>
    <groupId>
     org.apache.maven.plugins
    </groupId>
    <artifactId>
     maven-checkstyle-plugin
    </artifactId>
    <version>
     2.11
    </version>
    <configuration>
     <consoleOutput>
      true
     </consoleOutput>
     <configLocation>
      checkstyle.xml
     </configLocation>
     <failOnViolation>
      false
     </failOnViolation>
    </configuration>
   </plugin>
  </plugins>
  <pluginManagement>
   <plugins>
    <plugin>
     <artifactId>
      maven-invoker-plugin
     </artifactId>
     <version>
      1.8
     </version>
    </plugin>
   </plugins>
  </pluginManagement>
 </build>
 <profiles>
  <profile>
   <id>
    default-profile
   </id>
   <activation>
    <activeByDefault>
     true
    </activeByDefault>
    <file>
     <exists>
      ${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar
     </exists>
    </file>
   </activation>
   <properties>
    <toolsjar>
     ${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar
    </toolsjar>
   </properties>
  </profile>
  <profile>
   <id>
    mac-profile
   </id>
   <activation>
    <activeByDefault>

     </exists>
    </file>
   </activation>
   <properties>
    <toolsjar>
     ${java.home}/../Classes/classes.jar
    </toolsjar>
   </properties>
  </profile>
 </profiles>
</project>

content.text:
Perfect! Now I understand the issue. The `compile-testing` library depends on `com.sun:tools` using a system scope dependency pointing to `${toolsjar}` which is set from the profiles. The problem is:

1. The parent `pom.xml` has profiles that set the `toolsjar` property based on file existence
2. With JDK 9+, `tools.jar` no longer exists (classes were moved into modules)
3. The profile activation fails, but the dependency still tries to resolve

Now I'll write my analysis and create the fixes. Let me write the analysis first:

input.content:
BUILD FAILURE ANALYSIS
======================

Repository: /home/travis/build/failed/google/auto

Build Command: mvn -B -U -f build-pom.xml verify --fail-at-end -Dsource.skip=true -Dmaven.javadoc.skip=true

ERRORS IDENTIFIED:
-----------------

1. Failed Module: auto-common (and subsequently auto-factory, auto-service)
   Error: Could not find artifact com.sun:tools:jar:11.0.27 at specified path /usr/lib/jvm/java-11-openjdk-amd64/../lib/tools.jar

ROOT CAUSE:
-----------

The project uses compile-testing library (version 0.7) which has a system-scoped dependency on com.sun:tools JAR.
In JDK 8 and earlier, tools.jar contained the Java compiler API and was located at ${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar.
Starting with JDK 9, tools.jar was removed as the compiler classes were integrated into the main JDK modules.

The parent pom.xml (at /home/travis/build/failed/google/auto/pom.xml) has profile configurations that:
- Activate when ${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar exists (default-profile)
- Set the toolsjar property to this path
- However, with JDK 11, this file does not exist

SOLUTION:
---------

Add a new profile in the parent pom.xml that activates for JDK 9+ and provides a dummy/alternative configuration for the toolsjar property. Since JDK 9+ includes the compiler API in the platform, we need to either:

Option 1: Add a JDK 9+ profile that sets toolsjar to a placeholder value with optional=true
Option 2: Add a profile that properly handles the absence of tools.jar for modern JDKs

The fix involves modifying /home/travis/build/failed/google/auto/pom.xml to add a profile that handles JDK 9+ where tools.jar does not exist.

FILES TO MODIFY:
----------------
1. /home/travis/build/failed/google/auto/pom.xml - Add JDK 9+ profile configuration

    <project.build.sourceEncoding>UTF-8</project.build.sourceEncoding>

          <artifactId>maven-invoker-plugin</artifactId>
          <version>1.8</version>
        </plugin>
      </plugins>
    </pluginManagement>

    <profile>
      <id>default-profile</id>

I see the artifact version is `11.0.27` which is coming from `${java.version}` in the compile-testing POM. The `systemPath` is being resolved to the old path. The issue is that even though I set toolsjar to jrt-fs.jar, the compile-testing POM has a hardcoded systemPath that uses `${toolsjar}`, but it's not getting the updated value properly. 

Let me trace back and see what's happening. Looking at the compile-testing-0.7.pom earlier, it has:
```xml
<systemPath>${toolsjar}</systemPath>
```

The `toolsjar` property should be `/usr/lib/jvm/java-11-openjdk-amd64/lib/jrt-fs.jar` but Maven is instead resolving it to the default path. This suggests Maven might be caching the effective POM or not reading the updated parent POM. Let me check if the sha1 hash needs updating:
